rows.text: A creature deck that wins by being the only person allowed to play Magic. Anafenza's second ability is the one that decides games: creature cards headed for an opponent's graveyard from ANYWHERE get exiled instead — milled, discarded, countered, wrathed. Against reanimator and graveyard value decks she is not hate, she is a hard lock, and she does it while attacking for four.

rows.name: Anafenza, the Foremost
rows.text: a 4/4 for three that exiles every creature card an opponent would put in a graveyard, from any zone. Their Entomb targets vanish, their looting does nothing, and the creature you kill never comes back. Play her early even when she is not "needed" — the exile is retroactive protection.

rows.name: Rest in Peace
rows.text: the symmetrical version, for the graveyards Anafenza does not cover — lands, instants, flashback, Underworld Breach. Your own plan never uses your graveyard, so the cost is nothing.

rows.name: Kunoros, Hound of Athreos
rows.text: nothing is cast from graveyards and no abilities are activated from them, plus a 3/3 vigilance deathtouch lifelink body that blocks anything.

rows.name: Dauthi Voidwalker
rows.text: unblockable, exiles what they would bury, and lets you cast one of the exiled cards for free. He also carries Shadowspear well.

rows.name: Talon Gates of Madara
rows.text: a land that exiles a creature for four turns. Free interaction out of the mana base, and it dodges the "no removal in hand" hands.

rows.name: Thalia, Heretic Cathar
rows.text: their creatures and nonbasic lands enter tapped. It slows every ramp and blink deck at the table by a full turn and blanks flash blockers.

rows.name: Gaddock Teeg
rows.text: no noncreature spell with mana value 4 or more, and no noncreature X spells at all. That is most wraths, most big draw spells and most of the format's finishers.

rows.name: Linvala, Keeper of Silence
rows.text: opponents' creatures have no activated abilities. Mana dorks, sac outlets, equip-and-swing decks all stop; yours keep working.

rows.name: Aven Mindcensor
rows.text: flash him in response to the fetch, the tutor or the Cultivate and they see four cards instead of a library.

rows.name: Alms Collector
rows.text: they draw exactly one extra card, and you draw with them. It shuts off wheels and Rhystic-style refills without costing you a card.

rows.name: Orcish Bowmasters
rows.text: punishes every draw engine the table has, and the Orc Army grows all game.

rows.name: Hallowed Moonlight
rows.text: the instant-speed answer to a reanimation, a token swarm or a blink turn — and the creatures it catches are exiled, not returned.

rows.name: Solemnity
rows.text: for the counter decks — energy, poison, suspend, Dark Depths, planeswalkers that tick up. Be aware it also blanks Anafenza's own attack trigger, so hold it until the +1/+1 counters matter less than what they are doing.

rows.name: Grand Abolisher
rows.text: opponents cannot cast spells or activate abilities during your turn. This is how a fair creature deck resolves its Craterhoof.

rows.name: Voice of Victory
rows.text: the redundant copy on a body that also makes a token every combat.

rows.name: Sigarda, Font of Blessings
rows.text: your other legendary creatures get hexproof and cannot be sacrificed — and this deck is unusually legendary-dense, so it covers most of the board.

rows.name: Flowering of the White Tree
rows.text: an anthem plus ward for that same legendary board, which turns spot removal into a mana tax.

rows.name: Teferi's Protection
rows.text: the reset button. Phase out through a wrath, a combo kill or a Cyclonic Rift.

rows.name: Heroic Intervention
rows.text: cheaper insurance against the wrath you can see coming.

rows.name: Veil of Summer
rows.text: one mana to beat a counterspell, a targeted removal spell or a discard spell, and it draws.

rows.name: Guardian of Faith
rows.text: phases your board out at instant speed and leaves a 3/3 behind.

rows.name: Reprieve
rows.text: not a counterspell, so it works under Teeg — the spell goes back to hand and they have to find the mana again.

rows.name: Swords to Plowshares
rows.text: one mana, exile, no conditions. With Anafenza on board the creature never reaches a graveyard anyway.

rows.name: Path to Exile
rows.text: same, and the land they get enters tapped under Thalia.

rows.name: Assassin's Trophy
rows.text: any permanent, two mana. The catch-all for the combo piece you did not expect.

rows.name: Anguished Unmaking
rows.text: instant-speed exile for anything nonland.

rows.name: Abrupt Decay
rows.text: uncounterable, and most of the format's problem permanents cost three or less.

rows.name: Krosan Grip
rows.text: split second, so it answers the thing they were going to protect in response.

rows.name: Aura Shards
rows.text: the ceiling. With a board of creatures, every single one that enters destroys an artifact or enchantment. It ends stax decks by itself.

rows.name: Toxic Deluge
rows.text: your creatures are cheap and theirs are not. Pay three, kill their board, keep most of yours.

rows.name: Damn
rows.text: a two-mana removal spell early and a wrath late, which is exactly the flexibility a hatebear deck wants.

rows.name: Nowhere to Run
rows.text: strips hexproof and ward first, then kills. The answer to the commander that says "can't be targeted".

rows.name: Elesh Norn, Mother of Machines
rows.text: your enter-the-battlefield triggers happen twice and theirs do not happen at all. Aura Shards, Loran, Manglehorn and Craterhoof all double; their blink and value decks stop cold.

rows.name: Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite
rows.text: a one-sided wrath that stays on the battlefield. Their board gets -2/-2, yours gets +2/+2, and your hatebears become real attackers.

rows.name: Loran of the Third Path
rows.text: an artifact or enchantment on the way in, twice with the other Norn.

rows.name: Manglehorn
rows.text: the same for artifacts, and the ones they keep enter tapped.

rows.name: Craterhoof Behemoth
rows.text: the standard ending. A board of bears that has been holding the table hostage is wide enough that Craterhoof is lethal to one player and usually two.

rows.name: God-Eternal Rhonas
rows.text: doubles the power of your other creatures and gives them deathtouch, which turns the same board into a kill without needing to go wide.

rows.name: Rhonas the Indomitable
rows.text: nearly unkillable, and the pump is a mana sink on a board that is already stalled.

rows.name: Ohran Frostfang
rows.text: everything you control has deathtouch and draws a card when it connects. Blocking becomes impossible and your attacks refuel your hand.

rows.name: Shadowspear
rows.text: trample and lifelink on the finisher, and it strips hexproof and indestructible from their blockers.

rows.name: Tymna the Weaver
rows.text: your cheap evasive bears connect with different opponents, so she reliably draws two or three.

rows.name: Toski, Bearer of Secrets
rows.text: indestructible, must attack, draws for each creature that connects. He survives every wrath you cast yourself.

rows.name: Sylvan Library
rows.text: with this much cheap interaction, paying life for the extra cards is nearly always right.

rows.name: Beast Whisperer
rows.text: a card for each of the creature spells that make up most of the deck.

rows.name: Tocasia's Welcome
rows.text: the same trigger, on an enchantment removal cannot easily reach, and it only counts the cheap ones — which is what the deck is.

rows.name: Esper Sentinel
rows.text: a tax they usually pay in cards rather than mana on turn one.

rows.name: Black Market Connections
rows.text: three mana into a Treasure, a body and a card each turn. Costs life, but this deck ends games before that matters.

rows.name: Eladamri's Call
rows.text: instant speed, finds the exact bear the table is weak to. Usually Linvala, Teeg or Craterhoof.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep mana dorks and cheap bears over expensive haymakers. Delighted Halfling, Bloom Tender and the one-mana elves are what let you deploy two hate pieces in a turn, which is when the lock actually starts.

Deploy the tax pieces in the order that hurts the table's fastest deck, not in mana order. Against combo, Grand Abolisher and Teeg come first; against a green ramp table, Thalia and Linvala; against graveyards, Anafenza and Rest in Peace.

rows.name: Anafenza, the Foremost
rows.text: cast her on turn three whenever you can. She is a 4/4 that starts a clock, and the exile clause is the kind of effect that is only worth anything if it is already on the battlefield when they try.

rows.name: Craterhoof Behemoth
rows.text: do not jam it into open mana. Grand Abolisher or Voice of Victory first, then the alpha strike — this deck has the pieces to make the last turn uninteractive.
